messages:
Carlos (support): FYI customer reported sudden p99 regression on hosted inference starting ~09:40 UTC. p50 unchanged, p95 up a bit, p99 jumped to ~3.4s. They see many queued requests and intermittent 429s. Repro steps attached from their side.
Carlos (support): Repro they ran: `hey --concurrency 40` against /v1/generate and get long tail. We correlate to queue_length metric on admit-controller. Dashboard: <https://console.redwood.example/d/admit/queues?org=astra|admit dashboard>
Carlos (support): Quick logs from their session:
```
2026-03-15T09:41:12Z INFO admit_controller: enqueue request tenant=astra queue_len=732
2026-03-15T09:41:12Z WARN worker_pool: worker vm-worker-07 cpu=86% queue_wait_ms=8200
2026-03-15T09:41:13Z ERROR api: returned 429 tenant=astra reason=admit_limit
```
Priya (oncall): thanks Carlos. Are we seeing cluster-wide impact or focused on a few worker pools/tenants? any recent deploys at 09:30-09:40? @deploy-bot did we deploy anything?
deploy-bot: rolled back recent commit `feat/batcher-tune` at 2026-03-15T09:37:58Z for service `admit-controller` (rollback id rbk-552).
Priya (oncall): ok rollback happened but customer still sees tail. I'm going to check admit metrics and per-tenant caps.
Sasha (eng-runtime): looking at metrics now — admit_controller.queue_length spiked across us-west-2 zone, but most of the backlog is on pool `vm-pool-7` serving mixed-tier customers. Per-tenant concurrency for `astra` is at their baseline (50). However noisy pattern: a handful of long-running requests are saturating workers and preventing batching.
Tess (eng-sre): suggestions for immediate mitigation: 1) temporarily reduce max_batch_size for pool vm-pool-7 to lower batch wait time 2) raise admission soft-limit for high-tier customers so they can bypass short queue 3) evict or restart the top CPU worker(s). Which do you want me to try first? :thinking_face: 
Priya (oncall): try (3) restart vm-worker-07 and (1) lower max_batch_size, in that order. I'll prepare an admin toggle for admission soft-limits if needed.
Sasha (eng-runtime): command to lower batch size (run from admin-api host):
```
POST /internal/pools/vm-pool-7/config
{
  "max_batch_size": 8,
  "max_batch_latency_ms": 30
}
```
Priya (oncall): executing restart now: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/vm-worker-07 -n runtime-us-west-2`
Priya (oncall): restart done, worker came back in ~26s. queue_length for pool dropped from 710 -> 120 in ~70s. p99 on hosted for tenant `astra` dropped from 3.4s -> ~850ms (partial improvement).
Carlos (support): customer acknowledges improvement but still sees spikes at high concurrency. They're hesitant to ramp down their traffic.
Sasha (eng-runtime): follow-up: we should enable model-fallback routing for `astra` so heavy requests hit a smaller quantized variant to lower per-token latency. Also enable prefix caching for repeated prompts. Can we toggle fallback for that tenant?
Tess (eng-sre): I'll schedule a per-tenant mitigation: temporarily raise their priority window (allow burst up to +20 concurrency) and enable fallback. But note cost implications. If they keep hammering we need to throttle noisy clients or ask for dedicated capacity.
Priya (oncall): I've toggled fallback routing for tenant=astra: `POST /admin/routing/fallback` payload `{"tenant":"astra","model":"gpt-small-q4"}` — applied. Monitoring now.
incident-bot: created incident INC-2026-0315-07 for cluster queueing/backpressure (priority: P2)
Sasha (eng-runtime): watch metrics: after fallback enabled p99 is ~420ms and queue_length ~45. Good effect. Recommend follow-up: 1) run async replayer on their traffic to build KV/prefix caches 2) propose Dedicated capacity or reserved pools for them if they want production SLA.
Carlos (support): passing mitigation notes to customer and recommending temporary traffic shaping client-side. They'll accept fallback for now and open a ticket to discuss Dedicated. :thumbsup:
Tess (eng-sre): action items for postmortem: capture timeline, root cause analysis (noisy long-running requests + suboptimal batcher defaults after last-week tuning), consider auto-eviction heuristics for stuck long requests, and a tenant-level backpressure policy with automatic isolation.
Priya (oncall): agreed. I'll leave monitoring hooks for 2 hours and then hand to eng-runtime to follow up with config changes. Thanks everyone.
Carlos (support): closing the customer escalation for now; will re-open if they see recurrence.
